one_liner: Senior DoD IT program manager at DMDC leading identity management and infrastructure modernization portfolios, including acquisition strategy, budgets, risk, and senior-executive advising.
fit_summary: This role requires a year of specialized experience at the GS-12 equivalent managing IT programs, which means project plans, performance metrics, cost/schedule/performance risk, and IT business cases. Daniel's IEM consulting background in emergency management and strong stakeholder skills are relevant to program work, but nothing on file shows IT program or acquisition experience. Daniel would likely be screened out unless the IEM work involved managing technology projects or systems.
eligibility: Open to the public and to military spouses, so Daniel can apply with no federal status.
Requires one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-12 (for GS-13) or GS-13 (for GS-14) in IT program management, and education cannot substitute.
You must be able to obtain and keep a Secret security clearance.
You must meet DAWIA Level III certification in the Information Technology career field within 24 months of appointment.
strategy: Before applying, confirm honestly whether your IEM work included managing projects with IT, data, or system components, such as grants-management platforms or recovery tracking systems. If it did not, skip this posting and target GS-0301/0340 emergency management or program analyst roles at GS-9 to GS-11.
If you qualify, describe the IEM work in the posting's terms: project plans, performance metrics, risk to cost/schedule/performance, and business cases, each with dates and hours per week.
Fit everything within the two-page USAJOBS limit, putting the most recent 12+ months of qualifying experience first and stating the specialized experience directly.
Highlight work advising government clients and senior officials, which maps to the stakeholder and consensus-building language.
The posting closes 2026-11-15 but may close early or have cutoffs, so apply early.
resume_bullets: Managed [number] concurrent projects for [government client] supporting [system/technology], developing project plans, tracking performance metrics, and delivering status updates to [audience].
Analyzed program requirements and identified risks to cost, schedule, and performance for [project], recommending mitigations that [result you can verify].
Briefed [senior officials/client executives] on [topic], building consensus on program objectives across [number] stakeholder groups.
interview_questions: Describe an IT project you managed from planning through delivery. How did you track cost, schedule, and performance?
How have you built a business case for a technology investment?
Tell us about a time you had to influence a senior executive who disagreed with your recommendation.
What do you know about DoD acquisition and DAWIA certification?
watch_outs: The core requirement is IT program and acquisition experience, and emergency-management consulting alone will probably not qualify.
DAWIA Level III IT certification within 24 months is a significant training commitment.
A Secret clearance is required, and the job is not remote despite telework eligibility.
